User is planning a large backyard BBQ with brisket, ribs, pulled-pork sandwiches, burgers, hot dogs, grilled pineapple, coleslaw, and other sides. They especially love mac and cheese. They recently bought a Weber gas grill and enjoy using it for quick weeknight meals. Their favorite BBQ sauce is Kansas City Masterpiece; they also previously considered Sweet Baby Ray’s. They appreciate practical, step-by-step BBQ guidance.

Brisket plan: 10–12 lb brisket at 225°F, trimmed of excess fat and silver skin, patted dry, binder optional, Killer Hogs BBQ Rub, post oak chips, water pan, fat-side up, vent/probe management, wrap around 4–5 hours based on tenderness/probe feel, then rest and slice against the grain. Do not treat 160–180°F as the tenderness endpoint.

Pulled-pork sandwiches: boneless pork shoulder/Boston butt, low-and-slow smoke, mild woods such as apple or cherry; hickory/pecan can work. Serve shredded pork on buns with coleslaw and pickles, with Kansas City Masterpiece or offer varied sauces.

trajectory: User is planning another backyard BBQ featuring ribs and brisket. Mac and cheese is a favorite for the user and friends. They plan to serve Sweet Baby Ray’s BBQ sauce with ribs. For brisket, they chose the Low and Slow Smoked Brisket recipe (10–12 lb brisket, 225°F smoker, rub, optional Sweet Baby Ray’s-style sauce) and plan to use post oak wood chips. They selected Killer Hogs BBQ Rub. Before seasoning, they plan to trim excess fat and remove silver skin, then pat dry, use a binder such as mustard, apply rub evenly, and let it rest before smoking. Smoker setup discussed: preheat to 225°F, use a water pan, add post oak via smoker box or directly to coals, place brisket fat-side up, manage vents, monitor temperature, and wrap after 4–5 hours when near stall/internal tenderness. Prioritize accurate probe checks, food safety, fire safety, and avoiding claims that 160–180°F determines tenderness; brisket is often taken much higher. User appreciates practical, step-by-step BBQ guidance.
